description: Virginia-only rules checked against the Code of Virginia and the Department of Motor Vehicles. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Except as otherwise provided, Virginia's maximum speed on interstate highways, other limited-access highways with divided roadways, nonlimited-access highways with four or more lanes, and state primary highways is
questions.explanation: Section 46.2-870 says that except as otherwise provided in the article, the maximum speed limit shall be 55 miles per hour on those highways. On other highways the maximum is 55 for a passenger motor vehicle, bus, pickup or panel truck, or motorcycle, and 45 for a truck or a vehicle towing a vehicle designed for self-propulsion or a house trailer.

questions.q: Virginia's 70 mph maximum applies where lawfully placed signs are erected after a traffic engineering study and analysis of accident and law-enforcement data, on
questions.explanation: Section 46.2-870 says the maximum shall be 70 miles per hour where indicated by lawfully placed signs, erected after that study and analysis, on interstate highways; multilane, divided, limited-access highways; and high-occupancy vehicle lanes if those lanes are physically separated from regular travel lanes.

questions.q: The maximum speed on Virginia highways in a business or residence district is 25 mph, except on
options: Every residential street if a sign says 35
questions.explanation: Section 46.2-874 says the maximum speed shall be 25 miles per hour on highways in business or residence districts, except on interstate or other limited-access highways with divided roadways, nonlimited-access highways having four or more lanes, and all state primary highways.

questions.q: A Virginia driver younger than 21 violates the underage driving-after-consuming-alcohol section when a chemical test shows a blood alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: Section 18.2-266.1 says it is unlawful for any person younger than 21 to operate a motor vehicle after illegally consuming alcohol. A person with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent or more but less than 0.08, by weight by volume or in grams per 210 liters of breath, is in violation of that section.

questions.q: If a Virginia driver age 18 or older accumulates 18 demerit points in 12 months, or 24 points in 24 months, DMV
options: Suspends driving for 90 days and requires a clinic
Revokes the license for one year in every case
questions.explanation: The DMV page for drivers age 18 and over says 18 demerit points in 12 months, or 24 points in 24 months, suspends the driving privilege for 90 days. The driver must complete a driver-improvement clinic before the privilege is restored, and is then placed on a six-month probation. Twelve demerit points in 12 months, or 18 in 24 months, requires the clinic but is not itself that suspension.

provenance.section: Traffic violations, drivers age 18 and over

questions.q: After a second demerit-point conviction for a violation committed when the Virginia driver was under 18, DMV
questions.explanation: The DMV page for drivers under 18 says that after the second demerit-point conviction, or a safety-belt or child-restraint conviction, for a violation committed under 18, DMV suspends the permit or license for 90 days. After a third such conviction, DMV revokes the permit or license for one year or until age 18, whichever is longer.

questions.q: Virginia assigns one safe-driving point for each full calendar year of violation-free driving, up to a maximum of
questions.explanation: The DMV points-system page says one safe-driving point is assigned for each full calendar year that the person holds a valid Virginia license and drives without any violations or suspensions. A driver may accumulate a maximum of five safe-driving points. Demerit points remain valid for two years from the date of the offense.

questions.q: The minimum age for a Virginia learner's permit is
questions.explanation: The Department of Motor Vehicles says you must be at least 15 years and six months old to apply for a learner's permit, and that no exceptions are made to that age. A first driver's license requires the applicant to be at least 16 years and 3 months old.

questions.q: A Virginia driver under 18 must hold a learner's permit at least nine months and certify driving of
options: 45 hours, 15 of which occurred after sunset
50 hours, 10 of which were in rain
questions.explanation: The DMV learner's-permit page says a driver under 18 must complete a state-approved driver-education program, hold the learner's permit at least nine months, and have a parent or guardian certify at least 45 hours of driving, 15 of which occurred after sunset.

questions.q: The licensed driver who must sit beside a Virginia learner's-permit holder must be at least 21, or
options: 18+ if a legal guardian or sibling
16 if the person has a provisional license
Any age if the trip is in daylight
questions.explanation: The DMV says a learner's permit lets you drive when a licensed driver is seated beside you, and that licensed driver must be at least 21, or 18 or older if the person is your legal guardian or sibling.

questions.q: Until the holder is 18, a Virginia provisional driver's license does not authorize driving with more than one passenger under 21. After the first year, up to three passengers under 21 are allowed when
options: A licensed driver 21+ sits beside them
questions.explanation: Section 46.2-334.01(B) limits a provisional licensee under 18 to one passenger under 21. After the first year, the holder may drive with up to three passengers under 21 when driving to or from a school-sponsored activity, when a licensed driver at least 21 occupies the seat beside the driver, or in an emergency. Those limits do not apply to members of the driver's family or household.

questions.q: A Virginia provisional driver's license does not authorize driving on a highway
options: Between midnight and 4 a.m., with exceptions
Between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m. with no exceptions
Between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. only in cities
questions.explanation: Section 46.2-334.01(C) says the holder of a provisional driver's license shall not operate a motor vehicle between midnight and 4:00 a.m. except when driving to or from work, to or from a supervised activity sponsored by a school or a civic, religious, or public organization, accompanied by a parent, a person acting in loco parentis, or a spouse 18 or older who is licensed and seated beside the driver, or in an emergency, including volunteer fire and emergency-medical response. Those restrictions expire on the holder's 18th birthday.

questions.q: A Virginia learner's permit does not authorize its holder to operate a motor vehicle
options: On a road with a speed limit above 45 mph
With a parent in the front seat
questions.explanation: Section 46.2-335(D) says no learner's permit shall authorize its holder to operate a motor vehicle between midnight and four o'clock a.m. Subsection (C) also limits the permit holder to one passenger under 21, with exceptions for an approved driver-education program and for members of the driver's family or household.

questions.q: In Virginia, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Virginia requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 9 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Virginia complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Virginia requires 45 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: Apply for a Learner's Permit | Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: Of a Virginia teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Virginia requires at least 15 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Virginia: 15 hours of the supervised driving at night.

questions.q: In Virginia, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Virginia, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years and 3 months.
questions.remember: Virginia: driving alone from 16 years and 3 months.

provenance.manual: Driver License Eligibility Requirements | Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In Virginia, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Virginia drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

provenance.manual: § 46.2-334.01. Licenses issued to persons less than 18 years old subject to certain restrictions

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Virginia car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Virginia car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Virginia, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Virginia brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Virginia, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Virginia residential district?
questions.explanation: Virginia sets 25 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

provenance.manual: § 46.2-874. Maximum speed limit in business and residence districts

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Virginia?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Virginia can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Virginia rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Virginia's law on drivers using a phone?
options: No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: Virginia: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: § 46.2-818.2. Use of handheld personal communications devices in certain motor vehicles; exceptions; penalty

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Virginia?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Virginia left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

provenance.manual: § 46.2-836. Left turn on steady red after stopping

questions.q: How is Virginia's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Virginia seat belt enforcement is secondary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Virginia?
questions.explanation: Virginia requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Virginia: car or booster seat until 8 years.

questions.q: What is Virginia's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Virginia requires at least $50,000 / $100,000 / $25,000.

provenance.manual: Insurance Requirements | Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: Under Virginia's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Virginia can suspend an adult's license at 18 points in 12 months.
